RESY

RESY assigns vegetation plots to vegetation or habitat types based on their plant community. A plot where beech, silver fir and beech-forest herbs such as wood sorrel grow together is a beech-fir montane forest. A plot where mat-grass (Nardus stricta) is abundant is an acidic grassland. RESY uses the species composition and cover or abundance recorded in each vegetation plot (relevé).

The rules for this assignment form an expert system (ESy; Bruelheide et al. 2021), stored as a text or JSON file. For each type, the rule specifies which groups of indicator species a plot must contain and how much cover they must have. In the example below, a plot is a beech-fir montane forest when beech and silver fir together cover more than 15% of it and beech-forest herbs more than 10%. You can also supply your own expert system.

RESY ships the expert system of Chytrý et al. (2020) for EUNIS (European Nature Information System), the habitat classification of the European Environment Agency for the land and sea of Europe. EUNIS defines a habitat by its plant and animal communities together with abiotic conditions. Some of its rules therefore also use site data, such as the ecoregion, the country or the position on the coast.

Each expert system uses its own list of species names. The EUNIS expert system, for example, uses the names of Euro+Med PlantBase, the taxonomy used in data from the European Vegetation Archive (EVA). Species names in plot data that follow another taxonomy, such as GBIF or World Flora Online, must first be matched to the names of the expert system. resy_resolve_taxa() does this for any expert system: it removes author names and looks up synonyms. The synonym table that comes with RESY links about 65,000 synonyms from six taxonomies (Euro+Med, World Flora Online, GBIF, Catalogue of Life, ITIS and NCBI) to the species names of the EUNIS expert system. For an expert system with other species names, you can supply your own synonym table, as shown in Match species names.

The RESY App runs RESY in your browser, without installing R. It classifies the example plots or your own files with EUNIS-ESy or your own expert system, and shows the rules behind each assignment.

⏬ Installation

The package is available on CRAN. Install and load it with:

install.packages("RESY")
library(RESY)

RESY is still under active development. You can install the development version from the GitHub repository using the following commands:

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github(
   "https://github.com/florian-jansen/resy",
   dependencies = TRUE
   )
library(RESY)

🚀 Usage

To classify plots, resy_classify() needs two tables:

  • A species table, with one row per species in each plot, giving the plot ID, species name and cover.
  • A header table, with one row per plot, giving the plot ID and any site data used by the classification rules.

This example uses the bundled plots from Tuscany and Apennine-test, a small expert system whose rules require no site data. The header table therefore contains only plot IDs, but resy_classify() still requires it.

library(RESY)

file <- system.file("extdata", "data_example_species.csv", package = "RESY")
species <- read.csv(file)
header <- unique(species["PlotObservationID"])

res <- resy_classify(species, header, scheme = "Apennine-test")
cand <- resy_candidates(res, top_n = 3, wide = TRUE)
table(cand$classification)
#> 
#>  ?  F FB  N NG NS 
#> 92 33  8  6 20 41

F, FB, N, NG and NS are the five vegetation types of Apennine-test. A plot marked ? meets no type’s rule and is not classified. Here, 92 of the 200 plots remain unclassified. In these plots, all four indicator groups have at most 4% cover, below the lowest threshold in the rules (5%).

Each type has a priority in the expert system. When a plot meets the rules of several types, it is assigned to the one with the highest priority. Each row of cand is one plot: the type it is assigned to, then the types whose rules it meets, highest priority first. Plot CX45 meets the rules of FB (beech-fir montane forest, priority 5) and of its parent type F (forest, priority 2), and is assigned to FB:

cand[cand$plot_id == "CX45", ]
#>    plot_id classification type_1 priority_1 type_2 priority_2
#>     <char>         <char> <char>      <ord> <char>      <ord>
#> 1:    CX45             FB     FB          5      F          2

resy_eval_plot(res, p = "CX45") shows the species and conditions behind this assignment. For EUNIS, the header table also needs site data such as the ecoregion and the country, which resy_harmonize_eunis() adds from the plot coordinates.

RESY accepts these column names, or names standardized to Darwin Core, a standard set of field names for biodiversity data. The example data stores species names in scientificName.

Column Also accepted
PlotObservationID PlotID, eventID
TaxonName scientificName, or any column set with species_col
Cover_Perc organismQuantity, with an organismQuantityType of "% cover"
Longitude decimalLongitude
Latitude decimalLatitude
Country country
Altitude (m) Altitude, or minimumElevationInMeters and maximumElevationInMeters (their midpoint)

🖥️ Functions

These are the main functions:

  • resy_harmonize_eunis() adds the site data EUNIS needs (ecoregion, country, coast, dunes) from the plot coordinates.
  • resy_check_taxonomy() checks which species names the expert system knows; resy_resolve_taxa() matches names from other taxonomies to them.
  • resy_classify() assigns each plot to a vegetation or habitat type.
  • resy_candidates() lists the assigned and candidate types per plot.
  • resy_eval_plot() explains the assignment of one plot.
  • resy_validate_esy() checks your own expert system, and resy_add_classification() makes it available to resy_classify().

An overview of all functions and data is given in the tab Reference.

📚 Papers and links

  • Bruelheide et al. (2021): the expert-system language that RESY implements.
  • Chytrý et al. (2020): the EUNIS expert system, its species groups and the habitat distribution maps.
  • EUNIS-ESy on Zenodo: the released versions of the EUNIS expert system.
  • FloraVeg.EU: descriptions of every EUNIS habitat type.

📝 How to cite

To cite RESY in publications, please cite the package together with Bruelheide et al. (2021), which describes the expert-system language RESY implements, and, when you use the EUNIS expert system, Chytrý et al. (2020).

Jansen F, Bauer M, Calbi M, Colling G (2026). _RESY: Vegetation Type
Expert Classification System_. R package version 0.3,
<https://florian-jansen.github.io/resy/>.

Bruelheide H, Tichý L, Chytrý M, Jansen F (2021). "Implementing the
formal language of the vegetation classification expert systems (ESy)
in the statistical computing environment R." _Applied Vegetation
Science_, *24*, e12562. doi:10.1111/avsc.12562
<https://doi.org/10.1111/avsc.12562>.

Chytrý M, Tichý L, Hennekens S, Knollová I, others (2020). "EUNIS
Habitat Classification: expert system, characteristic species
combinations and distribution maps of European habitats." _Applied
Vegetation Science_, *23*, 648-675. doi:10.1111/avsc.12519
<https://doi.org/10.1111/avsc.12519>.
